mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of instances where RSAFS increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a month signals supply chain disruptions or reduced manufacturing output, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO declines by more than 2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL below 2% for 3 consecutive months) signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls simultaneously
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) combined with a rise in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals robust economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of instances where HOUST and RSAFS both increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months signals strong supply-side growth, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of instances where INDPRO increases for three consecutive months.
